transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-03-10 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (CISO, Cedar Tech), Maya Chen (Lead DevOps), Tom Park (Security Engineer), Sofia Alvarez (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Cedar Tech wants to understand Redwood's security posture for potential Dedicated/private deployment; also evaluating hosted for non-PII workloads. Action items and doc requests captured.

00:00 Jordan Mills: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um, appreciate it. i'm jordan (AE) and with me is priya from our security and infra team. quick confirm, alex, are we still around 48 minutes?
00:08 Alex Rivera: yep, that works. we'll try to keep Qs for the end, but feel free to interrupt.
00:12 Priya Kapoor: hi! short agenda, we'll run through compliance posture (soc2/iso), auth (sso/saml) and key mgmt, then deployment options and next steps.
00:20 Alex Rivera: perfect. high level — cedar is evaluating three paths: 1) hosted for prototypes, 2) dedicated for prod inference, and 3) private vpc/on-prem for regulated data. security is non-negotiable.
00:33 Jordan Mills: totally. can you give us a sense of your compliance baseline? are you already SOC2 or ISO required by customers?
00:39 Alex Rivera: we need SOC2 Type 2 within vendor stack and iso27001 is strongly preferred for some customers in europe. also strict data residency for eu customers.
00:48 Maya Chen: and we have SSO via SAML with Okta, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC needs to map to our internal roles.
00:55 Priya Kapoor: great, that's inline with many of our accounts. quick answer: redwood is SOC 2 Type II audited, we maintain an ISO27001 statement of applicability — i'll send the certs — and we offer SSO via SAML + SCIM. for dedicated/private we can ship a private control plane and support customer-managed kms.
01:10 Tom Park: when you say customer-managed kms, do you support HSM-backed keys or is it cloud KMS only?
01:16 Priya Kapoor: we integrate with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we support BYOK with HSM-backed keys if the customer brings them to their cloud account. for private on-prem installs we can connect to on-prem hsm via standard connectors, though that is scoped in the private deployment contract.
01:33 Alex Rivera: any gotchas around tokenization or logs containing sensitive tokens? we need assurance that audit logs don't leak secrets and that we can mask tokens.
01:41 Priya Kapoor: good question. we redact tokens at ingest and our audit logs are structured to remove secrets. we also support configurable redaction rules and field-level masking. we'll provide our logging schema and examples.
01:54 Sofia Alvarez: procurement will need DTAs and a dpa, what's the turnaround?
01:58 Jordan Mills: typical turnaround is 3–5 business days to start paperwork; we'll kick off the DPA and if needed, attach SOC2/ISO evidence under NDA.
02:06 Alex Rivera: okay. on retention — what's the default data retention and can we set shorter retention windows or auto-delete?
02:12 Priya Kapoor: hosted defaults to 30 days for request-level metadata and 90 days for aggregated telemetry, but we can set per-customer retention policies. for dedicated/private we can configure zero retention for request data and support immediate deletion workflows. we also offer customer-managed object stores for logs/artifacts so you control lifecycle policies.
02:28 Maya Chen: for the hosted path, do you support data residency (EU-only) endpoints?
02:32 Jordan Mills: yes, we have region-specific endpoints; EU-hosted accounts stay in eu regions and we can provide a data flow diagram. for full regulatory customers we typically recommend Dedicated or Private to ensure isolation.
02:44 Tom Park: can you walk through RBAC? we need role separation — devs can't access prod model keys, ops can...
02:50 Priya Kapoor: our platform supports hierarchical RBAC: org -> team -> project -> route. roles are mapped to SAML groups via SCIM and you can create custom roles. audit logs record admin actions and key usage.
03:05 Alex Rivera: about audit logs — is there an immutable logs option? tamper-evidence?
03:10 Priya Kapoor: for Dedicated we offer write-once logs to a customer-managed S3 with object lock (if enabled) and we can forward to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). immutable retention is possible via your storage configurations.
03:22 Jordan Mills: quick interjection — do you plan to run red-team or pen tests? some of our customers require third-party pen test evidence.
03:28 Alex Rivera: yes, exactly.
03:29 Priya Kapoor: we do annual third-party penetration tests and will provide summary reports under NDA. for Dedicated/private we can facilitate on-site audit support and coordinate evidence collection.
03:42 Maya Chen: network architecture: if we go dedicated in our cloud, what's peering/egress setup? will we need a public internet egress for model updates?
03:49 Priya Kapoor: typically we establish VPC peering or PrivateLink between Redwood compute and your VPC. model updates can be pulled over private links; only initial provisioning might require access to our model catalog. for strict air-gapped setups we have an on-prem package that includes model bundles, and updates are handled via controlled transfer.
04:06 Tom Park: interested — latency targets for dedicated? we need sub-200ms p99 for 2k qps workload.
04:12 Jordan Mills: performance sheet and verified benchmarks vary by model and instance type — priya will run the benchmarks with a sample workload in the follow-up POC.
04:19 Alex Rivera: what about encryption in transit? and for KV cache — is that encrypted at rest?
04:23 Priya Kapoor: all traffic is TLS 1.2+; for Dedicated/private, TLS mTLS is supported. KV cache and model artifacts are encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys (CMKs) when requested.
04:36 Sofia Alvarez: pricing question — if we commit to a dedicated pool, what are the SLAs?
04:40 Jordan Mills: dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency commitments; exact terms depend on commit size. we'll share the SLA doc in the follow-up.
04:46 Alex Rivera: do you have SOC 2 for your hosted control plane and also for the dedicated offering?
04:50 Priya Kapoor: yes, our SOC2 covers the hosted control plane; for Dedicated we include the compute runtime under the scope for customers on contracts and provide additional attestation language. again, we'll send the SOC2 Type II PDF.
05:02 Maya Chen: small transcription glitch — in previous calls i heard something about model quantization and potential quality regressions if you use 4-bit. we need guarantees for output quality after quantization.
05:10 Priya Kapoor: we have a model QA and regression framework; we run eval suites against quantized variants and recommend profiles per workload. in POC we can run your prompt set and show delta metrics.
05:20 Tom Park: are there any known issues with SAML group mapping delays or SCIM provisioning slowness? we've seen 15–20 minute delays in other vendors which causes access issues during rollouts.
05:30 Priya Kapoor: SCIM provisioning in our platform is near real-time for most providers; in rare cases it's eventual consistent, but we surface provisioning state in the audit logs so you can detect anomalies. we'll include SCIM logs examples in the doc drop.
05:45 Alex Rivera: if we do private on-prem, is the control plane still managed or do we get a fully customer-managed control plane?
05:51 Priya Kapoor: for private we provide an option: managed control plane within your VPC (Redwood manages upgrades) or fully customer-managed on-prem control plane (we provide orchestration manifests and a support contract). both options include audit and key integrations.
06:04 Jordan Mills: OK, sounds like we have good alignment. next steps: we'll send the certs and diagrams, and schedule a deep technical session for benchmarks. any other blockers?
06:13 Alex Rivera: procurement will need an initial quote and legal will want the DPA template. also need to ensure EU data residency controls are explicitly called out.
06:22 Sofia Alvarez: timeline — we're aiming to pick a vendor by end of Q2, so this is relatively urgent.
06:28 Jordan Mills: understood. we'll prioritize SOC2 + ISO + DPA. priya will own the technical follow-up.
06:33 Priya Kapoor: i'll reach out to schedule the benchmark call and will prep a deployment diagram and SCIM examples.
06:39 Tom Park: one last technical — when you redact tokens, do you also obfuscate partial prompt context shared across requests in cache? we can't have PII persist in kv cache.
06:48 Priya Kapoor: yes, we support configurable prefix caching and allow disabling kv caching for sensitive routes. we also offer token-level redaction before cache writes.
06:57 Alex Rivera: good — thanks everyone. let's wrap.

End of transcript.
